vsm1.4:42.0: The Ten Kinds of Skill in Absorption
vsm1.4:42.1: However, if this does not happen while he is practicing in this way,
vsm1.4:42.2: then he should have recourse to the ten kinds of skill in absorption.
vsm1.4:42.4: Skill in absorption needs to be dealt with in ten aspects:
vsm1.4:42.8: (4) he exerts the mind on an occasion when it should be exerted,
vsm1.4:42.9: (5) he restrains the mind on an occasion when it should be restrained,
vsm1.4:42.10: (6) he encourages the mind on an occasion when it should be encouraged,
vsm1.4:42.11: (7) he looks on at the mind with equanimity when it should be looked on at with equanimity,
vsm1.4:42.12: (8) avoidance of unconcentrated persons, (9) cultivation of concentrated persons, (10) resoluteness upon that (concentration).
vsm1.4:43.1: Herein, making the basis clean is cleansing the internal and the external basis.
vsm1.4:43.2: For when his head hair, nails and body hair are long,
vsm1.4:43.3: or when the body is soaked with sweat,
vsm1.4:43.4: then the internal basis is unclean and unpurified.
vsm1.4:43.5: But when an old dirty smelly robe is worn or when the lodging is dirty, then the external basis is unclean and unpurified.
vsm1.4:43.6: When the internal and external bases are unclean,
vsm1.4:43.7: then the knowledge in the consciousness and consciousness-concomitants that arise is unpurified,
vsm1.4:43.8: like the light of a lamp’s flame that arises with an unpurified lamp-bowl, wick and oil as its support;
vsm1.4:43.9: formations do not become evident to one who tries to comprehend them with unpurified knowledge,
vsm1.4:43.10: and when he devotes himself to his meditation subject,
vsm1.4:43.11: it does not come to growth, increase and fulfilment.
vsm1.4:44.1: But when the internal and external bases are clean,
vsm1.4:44.2: then the knowledge in the consciousness and consciousness-concomitants that arise is clean and purified,
vsm1.4:44.3: like the light of a lamp’s flame that arises with a purified lamp bowl, wick and oil as its support;
vsm1.4:44.4: formations become evident to one who tries to comprehend them with purified knowledge,
vsm1.4:44.5: and as he devotes himself to his meditation subject,
vsm1.4:44.6: it comes to growth, increase and fulfilment.
vsm1.4:45.1: Maintaining balanced faculties is equalizing the five faculties of faith and the rest.
vsm1.4:45.2: For if his faith faculty is strong and the others weak,
vsm1.4:45.3: then the energy faculty cannot perform its function of exerting,
vsm1.4:45.4: the mindfulness faculty its function of establishing,
vsm1.4:45.5: the concentration faculty its function of not distracting,
vsm1.4:45.6: and the understanding faculty its function of seeing.
vsm1.4:45.7:
So in that case the faith faculty should be modified either by reviewing the individual
essences of the states concerned, that is, the objects of attention
vsm1.4:45.8: or by not giving them attention in the way in which the faith faculty became too strong.
vsm1.4:45.9: And this is illustrated by the story of the Elder Vakkali (S III 119).
vsm1.4:46.1: Then if the energy faculty is too strong,
vsm1.4:46.2: the faith faculty cannot perform its function of resolving,
vsm1.4:46.3: nor can the rest of the faculties perform their several functions.
vsm1.4:46.4: So in that case the energy faculty should be modified by developing tranquillity, and so on.
vsm1.4:46.5: And this should be illustrated by the story of the Elder Soṇa (Vin I 179–85; A III 374–76).
vsm1.4:46.6: So too with the rest; for it should be understood that when anyone of them is too strong
vsm1.4:46.7: the others cannot perform their several functions.
vsm1.4:47.1: However, what is particularly recommended is balancing faith with understanding, and concentration with energy.
vsm1.4:47.2: For one strong in faith and weak in understanding has confidence uncritically and groundlessly.
vsm1.4:47.3: One strong in understanding and weak in faith
vsm1.4:47.4: errs on the side of cunning
vsm1.4:47.5: and is as hard to cure as one sick of a disease caused by medicine.
vsm1.4:47.6: With the balancing of the two a man has confidence only when there are grounds for it.
vsm1.4:47.7: Then idleness overpowers one strong in concentration and weak in energy, since concentration favours idleness.
vsm1.4:47.8: Agitation overpowers one strong in energy and weak in concentration, since energy favours agitation.
vsm1.4:47.9: But concentration coupled with energy cannot lapse into idleness,
vsm1.4:47.10: and energy coupled with concentration cannot lapse into agitation.
vsm1.4:47.11: So these two should be balanced;
vsm1.4:47.12: for absorption comes with the balancing of the two.
vsm1.4:48.1: Again, concentration and faith should be balanced. One working on concentration needs strong faith,
vsm1.4:48.2: since it is with such faith and confidence that he reaches absorption.
vsm1.4:48.3: Then there is balancing of concentration and understanding. One working on concentration needs strong unification,
vsm1.4:48.4: since that is how he reaches absorption;
vsm1.4:48.5: and one working on insight needs strong understanding,
vsm1.4:48.6: since that is how he reaches penetration of characteristics;
vsm1.4:48.7: but with the balancing of the two he reaches absorption as well.
vsm1.4:49.1: Strong mindfulness, however, is needed in all instances;
vsm1.4:49.2: for mindfulness protects the mind from lapsing into agitation through faith, energy and understanding, which favour agitation,
vsm1.4:49.3: and from lapsing into idleness through concentration, which favours idleness.
vsm1.4:49.4: So it is as desirable in all instances as a seasoning of salt in all sauces, as a prime minister in all the king’s business.
vsm1.4:49.5: Hence it is said in the commentaries (D-a 788, M-a I 292, etc):
vsm1.4:49.6: “And mindfulness has been called universal by the Blessed One.
vsm1.4:49.8: Because the mind has mindfulness as its refuge,
vsm1.4:49.9: and mindfulness is manifested as protection,
vsm1.4:49.10: and there is no exertion and restraint of the mind without mindfulness.”
vsm1.4:50.1: Skill in the sign is skill in producing the as yet unproduced sign of unification of mind through the earth kasiṇa, etc.;
vsm1.4:50.2: and it is skill in developing the sign when produced,
vsm1.4:50.3: and skill in protecting the sign when obtained by development.
vsm1.4:50.4: The last is what is intended here.
vsm1.4:51.1: How does he exert the mind on an occasion when it should be exerted?
vsm1.4:51.2: When his mind is slack with over-laxness of energy, etc.,
vsm1.4:51.3: then, instead of developing the three enlightenment factors beginning with tranquillity,
vsm1.4:51.4: he should develop those beginning with investigation-of-states.
vsm1.4:51.5: For this is said by the Blessed One:
vsm1.4:51.6: “Bhikkhus, suppose a man wanted to make a small fire burn up,
vsm1.4:51.7: and he put wet grass on it,
vsm1.4:51.12: would that man be able to make the small fire burn up?”
vsm1.4:51.14: —“So too, bhikkhus, when the mind is slack,
vsm1.4:51.15: that is not the time to develop the tranquillity enlightenment factor,
vsm1.4:51.18: Why is that? Because a slack mind cannot well be roused by those states.
vsm1.4:51.20: that is the time to develop the investigation-of-states enlightenment factor,
vsm1.4:51.23: Why is that? Because a slack mind can well be roused by those states.”
vsm1.4:51.24: “Bhikkhus, suppose a man wanted to make a small fire burn up,
vsm1.4:51.25: and he put dry grass on it,
vsm1.4:51.28: blew on it with his mouth,
vsm1.4:51.29: and did not scatter dust on it,
vsm1.4:51.30: would that man be able to make that small fire burn up?”
vsm1.4:52.1:
And here the development of the investigation-of-states enlightenment factor, etc.,
should be understood as the nutriment for each one respectively,
vsm1.4:52.3: “Bhikkhus, there are profitable and unprofitable states,
vsm1.4:52.6: dark and bright states the counterpart of each other.
vsm1.4:52.8: is the nutriment for the arising of the unarisen investigation-of-states enlightenment factor,
vsm1.4:52.9: or leads to the growth, fulfilment, development and perfection of the arisen investigation-of-states enlightenment factor.”
vsm1.4:52.10: Likewise: “Bhikkhus there is the element of initiative, the element of launching, and the element of persistence.
vsm1.4:52.12: is the nutriment for the arising of the unarisen energy enlightenment factor,
vsm1.4:52.13: or leads to the growth, fulfilment, development and perfection of the arisen energy enlightenment factors.”
vsm1.4:52.14: Likewise: “Bhikkhus, there are states productive of the happiness enlightenment factor.
vsm1.4:52.16: is the nutriment for the arising of the unarisen happiness enlightenment factor,
vsm1.4:52.17: or leads to the growth, fulfilment, development and perfection of the arisen happiness enlightenment factor” (S V 104).
vsm1.4:53.1:
Herein, wise attention given to the profitable, etc., is attention occurring in penetration of individual
essences and of the three general characteristics.
vsm1.4:53.2:
Wise attention given to the element of initiative, etc., is attention
occurring in the arousing of the element of initiative, and so on.
vsm1.4:53.3: Herein, initial energy is called the element of initiative.
vsm1.4:53.4: The element of launching is stronger than that because it launches out from idleness.
vsm1.4:53.5: The element of persistence is still stronger than that because it goes on persisting in successive later stages.
vsm1.4:53.6: States productive of the happiness enlightenment factor is a name for happiness itself;
vsm1.4:53.7: and attention that arouses that is wise attention.
vsm1.4:54.1: There are, besides, seven things that lead to the arising of the investigation-of-states enlightenment factor:
vsm1.4:54.7: (vi) reviewing the field for the exercise of profound knowledge,
vsm1.4:54.8: (vii) resoluteness upon that investigation of states.
vsm1.4:55.1: Eleven things lead to the arising of the energy enlightenment factor:
vsm1.4:55.2: (i) reviewing the fearfulness of the states of loss such as the hell realms, etc.,
vsm1.4:55.3: (ii) seeing benefit in obtaining the mundane and supramundane distinctions dependent on energy,
vsm1.4:55.4:
(iii) reviewing the course of the journey to be travelled thus: “The path taken by the Buddhas,
Paccekabuddhas, and the great disciples has to be taken by me, and it cannot be taken by an idler,”
vsm1.4:55.5: (iv) being a credit to the alms food by producing great fruit for the givers,
vsm1.4:55.6:
(v) reviewing the greatness of the Master thus: “My Master praises the energetic, and this unsurpassable
Dispensation that is so helpful to us is honoured in the practice, not otherwise,”
vsm1.4:55.7:
(vi) reviewing the greatness of the heritage thus: “It is the great heritage called the Good
Dhamma that is to be acquired by me, and it cannot be acquired by an idler,”
vsm1.4:55.8: (vii) removing stiffness and torpor by attention to perception of light, change of postures, frequenting the open air, etc.,
vsm1.4:56.1: Eleven things lead to the arising of the happiness enlightenment factor:
vsm1.4:56.2:
the recollections (i) of the Buddha, (ii) of the Dhamma, (iii) of the Sangha,
(iv) of virtue, (v) of generosity, and (vi) of deities,
vsm1.4:56.6: (x) reviewing encouraging discourses, (xi) resoluteness upon that happiness.
vsm1.4:56.7: So by arousing these things in these ways he develops the investigation-of-states enlightenment factor, and the others.
vsm1.4:56.8: This is how he exerts the mind on an occasion when it should be exerted.
vsm1.4:57.1: How does he restrain the mind on an occasion when it should be restrained?
vsm1.4:57.2: When his mind is agitated through over-energeticness, etc.,
vsm1.4:57.3: then, instead of developing the three enlightenment factors beginning with investigation-of-states,
vsm1.4:57.4: he should develop those beginning with tranquillity;
vsm1.4:57.5: for this is said by the Blessed One:
vsm1.4:57.6: “Bhikkhus, suppose a man wanted to extinguish a great mass of fire,
vsm1.4:57.7: and he put dry grass on it …
vsm1.4:57.8: and did not scatter dust on it,
vsm1.4:57.9: would that man be able to extinguish that great mass of fire?”
vsm1.4:57.11: —“So too, bhikkhus, when the mind is agitated,
vsm1.4:57.12: that is not the time to develop the investigation-of-states enlightenment factor,
vsm1.4:57.15: Why is that? Because an agitated mind cannot well be quieted by those states.
vsm1.4:57.17: that is the time to develop the tranquillity enlightenment factor,
vsm1.4:57.20: Why is that? Because an agitated mind can well be quieted by those states.”
vsm1.4:57.21: “Bhikkhus, suppose a man wanted to extinguish a great mass of fire,
vsm1.4:57.22: and he put wet grass on it …
vsm1.4:57.24: would that man be able to extinguish that great mass of fire?”
vsm1.4:58.1:
And here the development of the tranquillity enlightenment factor, etc.,
should be understood as the nutriment for each one respectively,
vsm1.4:58.3: “Bhikkhus, there is bodily tranquillity and mental tranquillity.
vsm1.4:58.5: is the nutriment for the arising of the unarisen tranquillity enlightenment factor,
vsm1.4:58.6: or leads to the growth, fulfilment, development and perfection of the arisen tranquillity enlightenment factor.”
vsm1.4:58.7: Likewise: “Bhikkhus, there is the sign of serenity, the sign of non-diversion.
vsm1.4:58.9: is the nutriment for the arising of the unarisen concentration enlightenment factor,
vsm1.4:58.10: or it leads to the growth, fulfilment, development and perfection of the arisen concentration enlightenment factor.”
vsm1.4:58.11: Likewise: “Bhikkhus, there are states productive of the equanimity enlightenment factor.
vsm1.4:58.13: is the nutriment for the arising of the unarisen equanimity enlightenment factor,
vsm1.4:58.14: or it leads to the growth, fulfilment, development and perfection of the arisen equanimity enlightenment factor” (S V 104).
vsm1.4:59.1:
Herein wise attention given to the three instances is attention occurring in arousing tranquillity,
etc., by observing the way in which they arose in him earlier.
vsm1.4:59.2: The sign of serenity is a term for serenity itself,
vsm1.4:59.3: and non-diversion is a term for that too in the sense of non-distraction.
vsm1.4:60.1: There are, besides, seven things that lead to the arising of the tranquillity enlightenment factor:
vsm1.4:60.7: (vi) cultivation of persons tranquil in body,
vsm1.4:61.1: Eleven things lead to the arising of the concentration enlightenment factor:
vsm1.4:61.7: (vi) encouraging the listless mind by means of faith and a sense of urgency,
vsm1.4:61.8: (vii) looking on with equanimity at what is occurring rightly,
vsm1.4:61.11: (x) reviewing of the jhānas and liberations,
vsm1.4:62.1: Five things lead to the arising of the equanimity enlightenment factor:
vsm1.4:62.2: (i) maintenance of neutrality towards living beings;
vsm1.4:62.3: (ii) maintenance of neutrality towards formations (inanimate things);
vsm1.4:62.4: (iii) avoidance of persons who show favouritism towards beings and formations;
vsm1.4:62.5: (iv) cultivation of persons who maintain neutrality towards beings and formations; (v) resoluteness upon that equanimity.
vsm1.4:62.6: So by arousing these things in these ways he develops the tranquillity enlightenment factor, as well as the others.
vsm1.4:62.7: This is how he restrains the mind on an occasion when it should be restrained.
vsm1.4:63.1: How does he encourage the mind on an occasion when it should be encouraged?
vsm1.4:63.2: When his mind is listless owing to sluggishness in the exercise of understanding or to failure to attain the bliss of peace,
vsm1.4:63.3: then he should stimulate it by reviewing the eight grounds for a sense of urgency.
vsm1.4:63.4: These are the four, namely, birth, aging, sickness, and death,
vsm1.4:63.5: with the suffering of the states of loss as the fifth,
vsm1.4:63.6: and also the suffering in the past rooted in the round of rebirths,
vsm1.4:63.7: the suffering in the future rooted in the round of rebirths,
vsm1.4:63.8: and the suffering in the present rooted in the search for nutriment.
vsm1.4:63.9: And he creates confidence by recollecting the special qualities of the Buddha, the Dhamma, and the Sangha.
vsm1.4:63.10: This is how he encourages the mind on an occasion when it should be encouraged.
vsm1.4:64.1: How does he look on at the mind with equanimity on an occasion when it should be looked on at with equanimity?
vsm1.4:64.2:
When he is practicing in this way and his mind follows the road of serenity,
occurs evenly on the object, and is unidle, unagitated and not listless,
vsm1.4:64.3: then he is not interested to exert or restrain or encourage it;
vsm1.4:64.4: he is like a charioteer when the horses are progressing evenly.
vsm1.4:64.5: This is how he looks on at the mind with equanimity on an occasion when it should be looked on at with equanimity.
vsm1.4:65.1: Avoidance of unconcentrated persons is keeping far away from persons
vsm1.4:65.2: who have never trodden the way of renunciation,
vsm1.4:65.3: who are busy with many affairs,
vsm1.4:65.5: Cultivation of concentrated persons is approaching periodically
vsm1.4:65.6: persons who have trodden the way of renunciation and obtained concentration.
vsm1.4:65.7: Resoluteness upon that is the state of being resolute upon concentration;
vsm1.4:65.8: the meaning is, giving concentration importance, tending, leaning and inclining to concentration.
vsm1.4:65.9: This is how the tenfold skill in concentration should be undertaken.
vsm1.4:66.1:
Any man who acquires this sign,
This tenfold skill will need to heed
In order for absorption to gain
Thus achieving his bolder goal.
vsm1.4:66.2:
But if in spite of his efforts
No result comes that might requite
His work, still a wise wight persists,
Never this task relinquishing,
vsm1.4:66.3:
Since a tiro, if he gives up,
Thinking not to continue in
The task, never gains distinction
Here no matter how small at all.
vsm1.4:66.4:
A man wise in temperament
Notices how his mind inclines:
Energy and serenity
Always he couples each to each.
vsm1.4:66.5:
Now, his mind, seeing that it holds back,
He prods, now the restraining rein
Tightening, seeing it pull too hard;
Guiding with even pace the race.
vsm1.4:66.6:
Well-controlled bees get the pollen;
Well-balanced efforts meet to treat
Leaves, thread, and ships, and oil-tubes too,
Gain thus, not otherwise, the prize.
vsm1.4:66.7:
Let him set aside this lax
Also this agitated state,
Steering here his mind at the sign
As the bee and the rest suggest.
